question: What operator recovery contract should OpenClaw support when a consented grouped update has already invoked a package installer or Gateway cron mutation and compensation cannot be proven complete?
rationale: The implementation can report `update_partial`, but choosing whether doctor, retry/reconcile, immutable operation identity, or a narrower no-apply policy is the supported product contract cannot be resolved mechanically from the patch.

options.title: Require recovery contract and live proof
options.body: Hold merge until the PR demonstrates exact package and Gateway failure/recovery paths and documents the accepted doctor/retry/reconcile flow.

options.title: Narrow the initial mutation scope
options.body: Ship only owners with fully recoverable local semantics and defer package-installer and Gateway cron mutation to a later explicit design.

options.title: Accept report-only partial state
options.body: Accept `update_partial` as the initial operator contract despite uncertain external compensation, with explicit maintainer ownership of that support burden.

recommendation.title: Require recovery contract and live proof
recommendation.body: Hold merge until the PR demonstrates exact package and Gateway failure/recovery paths and documents the accepted doctor/retry/reconcile flow.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review identifies the exact unresolved recovery and capability-escalation decisions.
